purpose: Deutetrabenazine is used to treat involuntary, repetitive movements that people cannot control. It helps with movements caused by Huntington's disease (called chorea) and also treats a condition called tardive dyskinesia, which causes uncontrolled facial and body movements often caused by certain psychiatric medications.
how_it_works: Your brain uses a chemical called dopamine to send signals that control movement. When there is too much dopamine activity in certain areas, it can cause those uncontrolled movements. Deutetrabenazine works by reducing the amount of dopamine released in the brain, which helps calm down those unwanted movements and gives you better control.
common_side_effects: Some common side effects include feeling sleepy or tired, feeling sad or depressed, having trouble sleeping, headache, dizziness, dry mouth, nausea, and diarrhea. Some people may also notice a slower heart rate or feel restless.
warnings: This medication carries a serious warning about depression and suicidal thoughts — please let your doctor know right away if you feel more sad, hopeless, or have any thoughts of harming yourself. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication. It should not be used if you have liver problems or if you are taking certain antidepressants called MAO inhibitors. Also tell your doctor if you have ever had depression or a heart rhythm problem.
typical_dosing: Most people start with a low dose — usually 6 mg once a day — and the doctor gradually increases it over several weeks based on how well it works and how you tolerate it. The maximum dose is typically 48 mg per day, split into two doses taken with food. Always take it exactly as your doctor tells you to.
